previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and severe neuropathic pain in the setting of type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis. She had not completed her dialysis the night before admission and presented with low sodium and poor oral intake. Workup showed no infection, with negative blood and peritoneal cultures. A gastric emptying study confirmed moderate to severe gastroparesis. She was treated with IV fluids, ondansetron, and erythromycin for gastroparesis, which improved over several days. For neuropathic pain and fibromyalgia, pregabalin was started and nortriptyline added, with gabapentin discontinued. She tolerated a gradual return to oral intake, had no emesis for over 48 hours, and was ambulating independently at discharge. She was discharged home with new prescriptions for pregabalin and nortriptyline, instructions to continue domperidone from her personal supply, and plans for outpatient EGD with botox injection. Regular EKG monitoring was recommended due to QT-prolonging medications.

(requiring multiple admissions), fibromyalgia who presents with 
shortness of breath and recent fall found to have hyponatremia.

# Dyspnea: Patient presented with subjective dyspnea but without 
any hypoxia or tachycardia. She does endorse atypical chest pain 
with tightness and ""soreness"" for several weeks and unable to 
characterize further. CXR without evidence of pneumonia or 
pulmonary edema. Does endorse dry cough and horseness in the 
setting of recent intubation and self-extubation at an OSH. 
Troponin negative x 3 and EKG without ischemic changes. Nuclear 
stress test done during admission was reassuring that patients 
dyspnea and chest pain was not cardiac in origin.

# UTI - patient with asymptomatic pyuria. Urine cltx grew > 100K 
GNR. Treated with 7 days course of bactrim for complicated UTI. 
Sensitivities of culture pending at discharge.

# Hyponatremia:  Found to have normal osmolality hyponatremia 
(calculated osm 270, measures 282) in the setting of elevated 
BUN and low Na. Patient unable to significantly concentrate 
urine given ESRD status and in the setting of poor PO intake 
without any NaCl and only drinking water all week this is likely 
poor solute intake ""tea and toast syndrome"". Na <20 in urine 
supported this. Improved to 130 at discharge. 

# s/p fall: S/p likely mechanical fall with no prodrome. CT 
C-Spine and CT head negative for traumatic injuries.  

# Constipation: Patient came in with significant constipation. 
She was treated with enemas x2 with some resolution prior to 
discharge.

# ESRD: PD was cont during admission.
#T1DM - continued on home insulin regimen without event.

CHRONIC ISSUES:  
# Gastroparesis: Continue home bowel reg with senna, Colace, 
bisacodyl, lubiprostone. Continue home nortriptyline  
# HLD: Continue home atorvastatin  
# Neuropathy: Continue home pregabalin, tizanadine  
# Hypothyroidism: Continue home levothyroxine  
# Fatigue: Continue home modafinil  
# Migraines: Continue home sumatriptan PRN  
# GERD: Continue home pantoprazole
